# Field two-track app: the go-live runbook

> Moved from `briangohr/HSBS` on 11/17/2026. Read `docs/build/README.md` first: the field contract wins, and the other team's exact list and column names are only in the old repo's copy.

Decision 119 (Brian, 11/14): every field piece is its own copy, proven on the private preview.
Decision 135 (Brian, 11/15): the field 7A and 7B copies are in the launch, so a field lead
names only field people and its closed reason is stored. This sheet is the order for taking the
copies live, after the preview pass. **Each step
needs Brian's go in chat, one step at a time.** Nothing here runs before that.

Who: **Brian** (Vercel settings and each go), **BB2** and **BB3** (flow steps), **BB1** (its
own flows, HSBS 2, 2B and 3), **Claude** (site code, checks, the record).

## The steps, in order

Each step lists its check and its rollback. Stop at the first failed check and roll back that
step only.

> **This site (`hsbs-hsd-field`):** the 1F address goes in `FIELD_FLOW_URL` only, on Preview
> and Production. `REFERRAL_FLOW_URL` and the routing in steps 1 and 2 below belong to the old
> site (`hsps-lifecycle`), which reached 1F through 1R. Here, step 1's check runs with the new
> address in `FIELD_FLOW_URL`, and step 2 does not apply.

1. **New 1F address (decision 130).** Done last, after the final bot test, at Brian's
   keyboard, with automatic screen captures off. The trigger's key is regenerated by the
   steps in Microsoft Learn, "Regenerate the SAS key used in HTTP trigger flows": the same
   flow keeps its run history, the address gets a new `sig`, and the old address stops
   working at once. In the same sitting the trigger's secure inputs setting is turned on and
   the flow saved (an import can't change a trigger's setting). Brian copies the new address
   from the trigger card into Vercel himself: the preview's `REFERRAL_FLOW_URL` for this
   step, and `FIELD_FLOW_URL` at step 6. The address and the sign-in token the Learn steps
   use are never written to a file, a chat or the desk. Check: the trigger card's `sig`
   differs from before; one TEST lookup on the preview answers 200; a call to the old
   address is refused. Rollback: none needed; the old address simply stops.
2. **Second preview pass, with go-live routing.** On the preview only, Brian sets
   `REFERRAL_FLOW_URL` back to the live 1R and `FIELD_FLOW_URL` to 1F (the routing in
   `src/lib/referral-app-flow.mjs`). Check: a TEST field key's lookup, submit and list work
   through 1R's "unknown key" answer, and an existing TEST link on the live 1R still answers
   exactly as before. BB2 records how long 1R's "unknown key" answer takes. Rollback: put the
   preview back on 1F directly.
3. **Part S: HSBS 2, 2B and 3 skip `Rep app` rows** (sheet F3, Part S, decision 103). A live
   edit to three of BB1's flows: one added trigger condition each, nothing else. BB1 gives
   its OK first. Check: each saved definition shows only that condition added. Rollback:
   remove the condition.
4. **The 3F copy goes live.** BB2 removes the copy's Test = Yes trigger condition and turns
   it On. The live 3F is not touched; it keeps every `FSC app` row. Check: the next TEST
   `Rep app` row (through the preview) gets one intro to the TEST inbox and one Service Case.
   **Wait for the first check before the TEST row.** After an import or a turn-on, the
   trigger does not see a change made before its first check. On 11/14 both misses came right
   after an import and both catches came without one (desk report 005, 11/15 12:10 AM). So
   wait until the first check shows in the run history's "Checks (no new data)" view, then one
   more minute, then send the TEST row. Pickup came from about 20 seconds to 5 minutes after
   a change; allow 11 minutes before calling a run missing. If it is missed, edit the row's
   Note once after the first check and wait again. Don't re-import to fix a miss: an import
   starts the trigger fresh again. After an import the details page may list only the Outlook
   connection; if the SharePoint connection's own page lists the copy, the connection is fine.
   **An import puts back whatever trigger conditions the package holds.** Import only a package whose trigger
   has no Test = Yes condition, never the 11/14 TEST build; and after any import at this
   step, read the saved trigger conditions back (Source `Rep app`, Route, Introduced On, the
   SystemEditAt rule, Intro Tries under 3, and no Test condition) before the check is
   repeated. A copy that still holds Test = Yes passes the TEST check and then starts on no
   real lead, while step 3 has already taken those leads away from HSBS 2, 2B and 3. Don't
   read anything into a quiet checks list. **Any import after launch** (a fix to the live
   copy) can miss a lead that arrives around it. After the first check, list Referrals for
   Source `Rep app`, Route `Direct to partner`, Introduced On blank and Intro Tries under 3,
   and edit the Note on each so the copy sees it. Turning the copy Off and On without an
   import doesn't need this: Learn says a polling trigger picks up where it left off.
   **The field gap check goes On in the same sitting** (sheet GC), if gate G12 passed.
   Nothing in it changes at go-live. First BB2 lists every `Rep app` row created after the
   gap check's start time with Introduced On blank. Each one gets its intro (the copy On,
   one edit to its Note, or Intro Tries set to 0 for a parked row) or goes to Brian. Then
   the gap check is turned On. From then, a field lead with no intro an hour after it
   arrived is in an hourly email to Brian, 7 AM to 9 PM Eastern. Check: its first run after
   turn-on ends Succeeded and its email step did not run (nothing to list).
   Rollback: turn the copy Off. The gap check can stay On; it only reads.
5. **1F stays On.** Check: one TEST lookup answers 200. Rollback: turn 1F Off (field links
   stop answering; nothing else changes).
6. **Production routing on.** Brian sets production's `FIELD_FLOW_URL` to 1F and confirms
   `REP_APP_ENABLED` is `true` on production, and that `REP_PAY_ENABLED` and `REP_PAY_PLAN`
   are **not** set on production (decision 137), then redeploys. Check: a TEST field link on
   production loads and its list works, it shows no dollar amount and no Earnings tab, and
   an existing link still answers as before. If
   the TEST field link says "This link does not work", check `FIELD_FLOW_URL` first: an
   address that is not https is skipped and shows only as one log line. Rollback: unset `FIELD_FLOW_URL` and redeploy; field keys go back to "This link does not
   work", and nothing else changes.
7. **The partner page moves to the 7A and 7B copies (decision 135).** Brian sets
   production's `PARTNER_LEADS_FLOW_URL` and `PARTNER_SAVE_FLOW_URL` to the copies, then
   redeploys. The copies already read every lead, so first BB2 opens each TEST partner link
   through the preview pointed at the copies and confirms each shows the same leads as
   today. Check, on production: the TEST HealthFirst partner page shows the TEST field lead;
   its sender line names the TEST rep by roster position and names no one outside the field build; a save sets
   its status; a lost save stores its closed reason on the Service Case; and BB2 reads that
   save's 7B run: it ended Succeeded, and it sent no email to anyone but the TEST inbox or
   Brian. An existing TEST lead that is not a field lead still shows and saves as before.
   Rollback: put the two addresses back and redeploy. No flow is edited either way.
   **7a. Deal value and stages on (decision 160).** In the same sitting, once the copies
   carry sheet DV (`docs/build/field-two-track-deal-value-stages.md`) and its TEST checks pass:
   Brian sets `PARTNER_STAGES_ENABLED=true` and `PARTNER_DEAL_VALUE_ENABLED=true` on
   production and redeploys. Check and rollback: sheet DV, "The one sitting".
   **7b. HealthFirst's contact becomes Kara (decision 129).** A live edit to two shared rows,
   on Brian's go, after BB1's OK: BB2 changes the HealthFirst Routing row's primary name and
   email, and the HealthFirst Partner Links row's name and email, from Rebecca Byrne to Kara
   Reyher, and rotates that Partner Links row's link key so the old link stops working. The
   new key is exactly 40 characters, each 0 to 9 or a to f, all lowercase, the format HSBS 7C
   makes. The partner page refuses any other key with "This link does not work" before it
   calls 7A (BB2's line 4, 11/15). The key is typed on the box and written nowhere. No
   flow is edited. From then every HealthFirst intro (other-team, FSC app and field), the partner
   page, the Friday partner email and the overdue nudge go to Kara. Check: both rows read
   Kara; the new key reads back as 40 lowercase characters of 0 to 9 and a to f; the new link
   opens the open HealthFirst leads; the old link doesn't open. Rollback: put the recorded
   values back and rotate the key again, in the same format.
8. **People go live** (build list rows 8 and 9): the roster load and sign-up, each person or
   batch on Brian's go.
9. **Clean up the TEST rows.** BB2 deletes, by ID, every TEST row from the build: the TEST
   partner row on Partner Links, the TEST people on Rep Roster and Team Roster, A136 to the
   last TEST referral (the hand-made R and G rows included), their Service Cases (case 105
   among them), the TEST SPIFF Ledger rows, the scratch list
   `F5 Check Referrals`, the Casey Check row and the flow `HSBS 1F check`. Check: a filter
   for TEST in each list returns only rows that predate the build.

## Rollback of the whole launch

In this order: if step 7a was done, unset `PARTNER_STAGES_ENABLED` and
`PARTNER_DEAL_VALUE_ENABLED` on production first; unset production's `FIELD_FLOW_URL` and
redeploy (step 6, one redeploy covers both); put the partner addresses back (step 7), turn the 3F copy Off (step 4). If step 7b was done, put the
recorded contact values back and rotate the key again. Part S can stay: it only stops HSBS 2,
2B and 3 from acting on `Rep app` rows, and no `Rep app` row is made once routing is off.

## Not in this launch

- **The qualify question on the partner page.** The field 7B copy launches with
  `EnforceQualify` off, and `PARTNER_QUALIFY_ENABLED` stays off (decision 96). Pay needs the
  qualify answer (decision 65), so both go on, in one sitting, before sheet F4's pay flow.
- **Three partner answers are not stored yet:** Stand, Talked on and Tried via. The page
  sends them on every save, and neither today's 7B nor the field 7B copy (built from it)
  writes them (desk report 008). The status, the meeting date, "talked to the doctor" and,
  on the field copy, the closed reason are stored. Brian decides when the three are added.
- **An update email to the rep.** On a field lead the 7B copy sends no update email at
  launch: its only update email went to the other team's sender, and a field lead has none. The rep
  reads the partner's status on the Track tab. Emailing the rep would be a new recipient
  and needs Brian's OK.
- The staffing branch of the 3F copy (sheet F3, Part B) and staffing in the app: Brian's
  later go.
- The F4 pay flow and real payouts: after launch, with real payouts off until Brian's go.
- Dollar amounts in the field app: off in production (decision 137). They show on the
  branch preview only, for checklist line 7. They go on in production after the pay flow
  writes real earnings, on Brian's go.
- "Reached" as "ever talked to the doctor" (a roll-up) instead of the current answer.
- In the 3F copy's roster position lookup: lower-case the rep's email and skip a Disabled
  Rep Roster row. 1F writes the email lower-case and refuses a Disabled rep, so the launch
  doesn't need it (desk report 005).
- **Before staffing is turned on in the app** (`REP_APP_COMPANIES` lists more than
  HealthFirst): SPIFF Ledger gets a Company column and a Practice Type column, and 1F's
  three ledger answers (earnings, a rep's rows on My Team, a manager's rows) read `company`
  from Company and return `practiceType` on staffing rows (contract F6.4). Today the ledger
  has neither column, so 1F reads `company` from Payer and leaves `practiceType` out. That
  is right only while every row is HealthFirst, where Payer and Company are the same word
  (desk report 004, Q-004-5; Codex flow review on PR 162). Checked with TEST staffing ledger
  rows before the switch.
- **Before any list 1F reads passes 4,000 items** (Referrals, Service Cases, Rep Roster,
  Team Roster, SPIFF Ledger; the largest was 85 on 11/14): every column 1F filters on is
  indexed, and its filtered Get items have pagination on. Past 5,000 items a filtered read
  can come back empty, and 1F would answer 200 with nothing in it (Codex flow review on
  PR 162). The item counts and index list go in the weekly check until this is built.
  BB2's read on 11/15 (desk report 040): the largest list is Team Roster at 703 items. None of
  1F's 12 Get items has pagination on. Four filtered columns aren't indexed: Service Cases
  Referral (both case reads filter on it alone), Team Roster Active (`field_5`), Rep Roster
  Status and SPIFF Ledger Payee Role. Two Top Counts can cut a list short with no error well
  before 4,000: the case reads (`Get_cases_rep`, `Get_cases_team`) at 100 and the referral
  list reads at 200.
